newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-THIRD ROUND SET OFF UNDER CLOUDY SKIES, THREAT OF RAIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THIRD ROUND SET OFF UNDER CLOUDY SKIES, THREAT OF RAIN.

text.p: Tom Lehman made a routine par on the first hole Saturday as he headed out for the third round with a one-shot lead at the U.S. Open.
The reigning British Open champion stood at three under par for the tournament on an overcast, humid day at Congressional Country Club that held the threat of rain.
Ten players were within three strokes of Lehman when he teed off, with four more players another shot back, including Masters champion Tiger Woods and first-round leader Colin Montgomerie of Britain.
Tied for second place, one shot off the pace, were Lehman's playing partners, 1994 U.S. Open champion Ernie Els and 24-year-old U.S. tour rookie Stewart Cink.
Conditions seemed good for scoring on the sprawling layout that has stayed soft from Friday's rain and the humid air on Saturday.
Among the early starters, Paul Stankowski, Billy Andrade and Olin Browne took best advantage by getting to three under par for the day early in their rounds.

Andrade, who birdied the second, fifth and seventh holes, hauled himself up to one under par, a status matched by Browne, who birdied three of his first four holes. Stankowski was at two-over for the tournament through 11 holes.

Others making early birdies included 1995 PGA champion Steve Elkington of Australia, who was two-under for the day through eight holes and two-over for the tournament, and Tommy Tolles, who birdied two of his first three holes to climb to one-under for the championship.
